why: A prefix the ratchet has never seen is a new leak and must fail the run.
A ratcheted prefix above its recorded count is a regression and must fail the run.
A prefix spelled like a prototype key must still be a new prefix, not an inherited ratchet entry.
An inherited Object property name must not read as a known prefix with an unbounded count.
A count that arrives as a string must still compare as over, not slip through a type mismatch.
A ratcheted prefix at its recorded count is the steady state and must pass.
Leaking fewer than recorded is an improvement and must pass.
A ratchet entry that leaked nothing is a notice, not a failure (environment variance between hosts).
